root_cause: /var/validation reached 100% full during the batch, so data-ingest's write of batch_1847_vectors.csv failed with ENOSPC partway through, yet ingest still marked the truncated file READY and the estimator turned its partial last row into NaN, which made the filter diverge.

evidence.note: /var/validation already at 95% (19.0G/20.0G) when the nightly run started
98% at 02:14:00; retention hook did not fire (trigger is 'over 98%')
Write of batch_1847_vectors.csv failed at offset 37104 with Errno 28 No space left on device
Truncated file (1180 of 1500 rows, 36.2 KB) still marked status=READY
Summary reports 0 errors because it only counts archive-side errors, hiding the local write failure
1847 dispatched to estimator-01 on the strength of the READY marker
estimator-01 read only 1181 rows (1180 complete plus 1 truncated) instead of 1500
Truncated row 1181 has empty field, filled with NaN
NaN measurement makes filter innovation non-finite at step 1181
Covariance non-finite; estimator aborts with 0 states emitted
Test 1847 FAIL: worker error 'non-finite result', states=0 expected=1500
Retention freed 6.1G only after the disk filled; later tests 1848-1850 exported and passed normally

ruled_out.reason: Happened on estimator-02, not estimator-01 which ran 1847; license reacquired with no task interrupted (line 168) and estimator-01 heartbeat was ok (line 166)
7 minutes earlier, a different failure mode (slow response, not non-finite output), and 1823 passed on retry with normal numbers
Different worker at 02:08; all estimator-02 tests passed
Different worker; affected tests 1806, 1826 and 1838 all passed
Remote read slowness at 02:04 and 02:10 (also line 70); those exports completed with full row counts, and the 1847 error was a local ENOSPC write failure
At 02:03:44 with no link-down or network errors near 02:15; ingest kept exporting normally
Same build on both workers; estimator-01 passed 1849 right after 1847 and 50/51 tests pass at ~3e-10 error; the NaN came from the truncated input
All components healthy and dispatch followed the parity policy; the scheduler acted correctly on the READY marker it was given
Corrections in the millisecond range, unrelated to file contents
